title: HMO Finance UK
h1: Not revealed. The search-result title for the URL is "HMO Finance UK" [a][b]; whether this is also the on-page H1 is unconfirmed.
summary: Silver Oak Capital's HMO Finance UK page presents the firm as an advisor that helps landlords work through the tiers of HMO lenders. It defines HMO finance as a specific mortgage product for properties let to three or more tenants who are not from one household, splits the market into small HMOs (up to 6 bedrooms) and large / sui generis HMOs (7+ bedrooms, or properties that require planning permission for change of use), states that standard buy-to-let lenders will not touch these properties so specialist lenders who understand licensing and management intensity are needed, and says the firm arranges lenders that use investment valuations so investors can recycle cash and pull out most of their deposit. Only search-engine summaries of the page were obtainable: headings, meta description, calls to action, process, fees, rates and full body text were not revealed. The third search (standard mode, 'criteria') returned only health-maintenance-organisation results and nothing about the firm.

sections.content: [b][seed] First-time landlords: options are limited since most lenders prefer you to have owned a standard buy-to-let for at least 12 months, but the firm works with several lenders who permit first-time landlords to buy HMOs, provided you have a strong personal income and a clear management strategy. faq.q: Can a first-time landlord get HMO finance?
faq.a: Options are limited since most lenders prefer you to have owned a standard buy-to-let for at least 12 months, but the firm works with several lenders who permit first-time landlords to buy HMOs, provided you have a strong personal income and a clear management strategy. [b][seed]

faq.q: What is the maximum LTV on HMO finance?
faq.a: Typically 75%, with some lenders stretching to 80% in exceptional circumstances, though rates increase significantly. [b][seed]

faq.q: Does an Article 4 direction matter for HMO lending?
faq.a: Lenders view Article 4 HMOs as more secure because supply is capped [b]; the seed first pass adds that an Article 4 direction can help valuations [seed].

faq.q: What counts as an HMO for finance purposes?
faq.a: A property let to three or more tenants who are not from one household; small HMOs are up to 6 bedrooms, large (sui generis) HMOs are 7+ bedrooms or need planning permission for change of use. [a][b]

faq.q: Can an HMO sit inside a portfolio loan?
faq.a: Specialist portfolio lenders are often comfortable with mixed portfolios containing HMOs [b]; a portfolio loan can sit alongside existing individual mortgages [seed].
